title: Speech by Hon. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (MP), Minister for Industry and Trade, during the World Competition Day Summit held at Serengeti Conference Hall, Competition House, Dar es Salaam on December 5, 2023.
title_sw: HOTUBA YA MHE. DKT. ASHATU K. KIJAJI (MB), WAZIRI WA VIWANDA NA BIASHARA WAKATI WA MKUTANO WA KILELE CHA SIKU YA USHINDANI DUNIANI KATIKA UKUMBI WA MIKUTANO WA SERENGETI, JENGO LA USHINDANI (USHINDANI HOUSE), JIJINI DAR ES SALAAM TAREHE 5 DISEMBA, 2023
text:
HOTUBA YA MHE. DKT. ASHATU K. KIJAJI (MB), WAZIRI WA VIWANDA
NA BIASHARA WAKATI WA MKUTANO WA KILELE CHA SIKU YA
USHINDANI DUNIANI KATIKA UKUMBI WA MIKUTANO WA SERENGETI,
JENGO LA USHINDANI (USHINDANI HOUSE), JIJINI DAR ES SALAAM
TAREHE 5 DISEMBA, 2023
Mwenyekiti wa Tume ya Ushindani (FCC) Dkt. Aggrey Mlimuka,
Wajumbe wa Tume (FCC),
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa FCC Bw. William Erio,
Mkurugenzi Mkuu Shirika la Viwango Tanzania, Dr. Athuman Y. Ngenya,
Mkurugenzi Mtendaji Kituo cha Uwekezaji Tanzania, Ndg. Gilead J. Teri,
Afisa Mtendaji Mkuu Wakala wa Usajili wa Biashara na Leseni (BRELA), Ndg.
Godfrey Nyaisa,
Wawakilishi wa Mamlaka ya Ushindani ya Jumuiya ya Afrika Mashariki,
Wawakilishi wa Trade Marks East Africa (TMEA),
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Shirika la Mawasiliano Tanzania,
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Shirika la Kuhudumia Viwanda Vidogo (SIDO),
Mtendaji Mkuu wa Wakala wa Vipimo (WMA),
Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa Shirikia la Maendeleo la Taifa (NDC),
Mkurugenzi Mtendaji wa Kituo cha Uwekezaji Tanzania (TIC),
Menejimenti na Watumishi wa Tume ya Ushindani,
Wawakilishi kutoka Wizara, Idara na Taasisi za Serikali,
Wawakilishi wa jumuiya za wachimbaji wadogo wa madini kutoka Kanda ya Ziwa,
Wawakilishi wa wazalishaji na wasambazaji wa mbegu kutoka Kanda ya Kaskazini,
Wawakilishi wa wakamuaji wa mchuzi wa zabibu na mafuta ya alizeti kutoka Kanda
ya Kati,
1

Wawakilishi wa wenye viwanda na wafanyabiashara kutoka Kanda ya Nyanda za
Juu Kusini,
Wawakilishi wa wakulima wa korosho kutoka Kanda ya Mashariki,
Wageni waalikwa,
Wanahabari,
Mabibi na Mabwana,
Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania!
Napenda nianze kwanza kwa kumshukuru sana Mwenyezi Mungu, mwingi wa
rehema na fadhili kwa kutujalia afya njema na kutuwezesha kujumuika pamoja kwa
ajili ya kushiriki shughuli hii muhimu ya kuadhimisha Kilele cha Siku ya Ushindani
Duniani inayofanyika kitaifa hapa Dar es Salaam.
Pili, nitumie fursa hii kuishukuru FCC kwa kunialika katika maadhimisho haya. Pia,
napenda kuwapongeza kwa maandalizi na uratibu mzuri wa maadhimisho haya ya
Siku ya Ushindani Duniani, hongereni sana!
Aidha, nitumie fursa hii pia kuwashukuru kwa dhati wadau na waalikwa wote kwa
kuitikia wito wa kuhudhuria shughuli hii muhimu ya kilele cha maadhimisho ya Siku
ya Ushindani Duniani kwa mwaka 2023, licha ya majukumu mengine mliyonayo,
tunawashukuru sana!
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, sisi sote tunafahamu kuwa lengo la
kufanya biashara yoyote ile ni kupata faida. Katika kufikia lengo hilo mbinu
mbalimbali hutumiwa na wafanyabiashara zikiwemo mbinu halali zinazosaidia
kuongeza ubunifu na kukuza biashara baina ya washindani na zile zisizo halali na
zisizo stahili yaani zile zinazokiuka sheria, kanuni na taratibu zilizopo ambazo ni
changamoto kubwa inayosababisha athari hasi katika ustawi wa biashara na
uchumi kwa ujumla.
Kutokana na changamoto hii, Baraza la Umoja wa Mataifa kupitia Uamuzi Namba
34/447 wa Disemba 19, 1979, katika kikao chake cha Aprili 8 hadi 22, 1980,
kilipitisha kanuni na Taratibu za Kudhibiti Vitendo Vinavyofifisha Biashara Duniani
(The Set of Multilaterally Agreed Equitable Principles and Rules for the
Control of Restrictive Business Practices). Kuanzia kipindi hicho, Kanuni hizi
2

zimekuwa chachu ya kuundwa kwa Sheria za Ushindani ulimwenguni kote chini ya
uratibu wa Shirika la Umoja wa Mataifa la Biashara na Maendeleo (UNCTAD).
Huu ndio ulikuwa msingi wa kuanzisha Maadhimisho ya Siku ya Ushindani Duniani
ili kukumbuka kuasisiwa kwa juhudi za kudhibiti vitendo vinavyofifisha ushindani
katika biashara ulimwenguni, kila ifikapo tarehe 5 Disemba.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, vitendo vinavyofifisha ushindani, ambavyo
ndio msingi wa sheria ya ushindani duniani kote vimegawanyika katika makundi
yafuatayo:
1. Makubaliano yanayofifisha Ushindani (Anti-Competitive Agreements).
Vitendo hivi ni pamoja na:
a. Washindani kukutana na kupanga bei za bidhaa na huduma;
b. Washindani kukubaliana kiasi cha bidhaa kinachozalishwa (output
restriction);
c. Washindani kugoma kupeleka bidhaa sokoni (collective boycott);
d. Washindani kukubaliana namna ya kuomba zabuni pale zabuni
zinapotangazwa (bid rigging);
2. Matumizi mabaya ya nguvu ya soko (abuse/misuse of market power) kwa
kampuni zenye hodhi kubwa ya soko.
3. Miungano ya kampuni yenye lengo la kuimarisha hodhi ya soko kufanyika na
kuathiri ushindani na walaji katika soko.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, kila mwaka katika kuadhimisha
maadhimisho haya huwa kunakuwa na kaulimbiu inayotuongoza. Kauli mbiu ya
mwaka 2023 ni “Prioritizing Socially Sensitive Sectors” ambayo kwa upande wa
Tanzania imetoholewa kuwa “Cartel and their harmful effect on consumers” yaani
“Njama baina ya washindani na madhara yake kwa walaji na watumiaji”.
Kaulimbiu hii imekuja wakati muafaka kwani dunia bado inaendelea kukabiliana na
madhara ya majanga makubwa mawili ya Uviko wa 19 “COVID-19” na vita ya
Ukraine na Rushia ambavyo vimesababisha kupanda kwa bei za bidhaa na
huduma. Hali hii inatoa tashwishi kwa wafanyabiashara kutafuta njia ya kuongeza
faida katika biashara zao kwa kila njama ‘cartels’.Jambo hili litaleta athari hasi kwa
uchumi na maendeleo ya Taifa na kukwamisha juhudi za Serikali ya awamu ya sita
3

za kuleta maendeleo endelevu kwa wananchi. Nitumie fursa hii kama Serikali
kuwataka wafanyabiashara kujiepusha na ‘cartels’ na FCC kama mamlaka ya
udhibiti “Regulator” kufuatilia kwa karibu hali ya soko.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, nimetaarifiwa kuwa katika kuadhimisha
siku hii, FCC ilifanya semina kwa wadau mbalimbali katika Kanda inayozisimamia
kama ifuatavyo;
(i) Wachimbaji wadogo wa madini katika Kanda ya Ziwa;
(ii) Wazalishaji na wasambazaji wa mbegu kutoka Kanda ya Kaskazini,
Arusha
(iii) Wakamuaji wa mchuzi wa zabibu na mafuta ya alizeti kutoka Makao
Makuu ya FCC - Dodoma,
(iv) Wenye viwanda na wafanyabiashara kutoka Kanda ya Nyanda za Juu
Kusini - Mbeya,
(v) Wakulima wa korosho kutoka Kanda ya Mashariki – Mtwara.
Aidha, nimefahamishwa pia wawakilishi wa wadau kutoka kila Kanda tajwa wapo
hapa ambapo kimsingi wanaitumia fursa ya maadhimisho haya kwa ajili ya
kujifunza na kujionea wenyewe jinsi changamoto wanazokutana nazo katika
maeneo yao zitakavyoshughulikiwa na FCC kwa mujibu wa taratibu zilizopo na kwa
mujibu wa misingi ya ushindani.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, Sheria ya Ushindani ina umuhimu mkubwa
sana katika kujenga uchumi. Hivyo Tukifanya biashara zetu kwa kufuata misingi ya
ushindani tutapata faida zifuatazo;;
(i) Kuongeza ufanisi katika uzalishaji na usambazaji wa bidhaa na huduma;
(ii) Kukuza ubunifu; ikiwa ni pamoja na
(iii) Kuboresha matumizi ya rasilimali kwa kuzingatia ufanisi.
Faida hizi zitatufanya tuweze kushindana katika masoko ya kikanda na kimataifa
ikizingatiwa kuwa Tanzania tayari tupo kwenye Soko huru la Biashara Africa yaani
AfCFTA. Hivyo, bila kufuata misingi hii Tanzania inaweza kuwa soko la bidhaa za
wenzetu.
4

Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, naamini tumesikia maelezo mazuri
yaliyobainishwa na Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa FCC kuhusu majukumu ya msingi
yanayotekelezwa na FCC katika kudhibiti na kusimamia soko la Tanzania bara
kuhakikisha kuwa washiriki wake hususan wafanyabiashara / kampuni
zinazoshindana kibiashara, zinazingatia misingi ya ushindani sambamba na haki za
mlaji.
Mkurugenzi Mkuu amesisitiza kuwa kula njama baina ya washindani kwanza ni
kinyume cha Sheria ya Ushindani na pia kuna athari kubwa kwa mlaji na mtumiaji.
Pia hali hii hufanya makampuni yetu yasiwe shindani kikanda na kimataifa kwani
hukosa ubunifu na ufanisi katika uzalishaji.
Sisi kama Serikali na Wizara inayoongoza na ambayo inasimamia biashara nchini
hatutapenda kuona wafanyabiashara wakila njama ama ya kupanga bei au
kupanga kiasi cha bidhaa cha kuingizwa sokoni kwani ni kinyume na Sheria ya
Ushindani na itakapobainika ni lazima sheria ichukue mkondo wake.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, Tanzania kupitia utekelezaji wa Dira ya
Maendeleo ya 2025, ilikwisha akisi mwelekeo wa Taifa wa kujenga uchumi imara
na wenye kuhimili ushindani wa kimataifa na kufikia lengo la maisha bora kwa
wote. Kupitia maono haya Serikali ikaanzisha vyombo vya udhibiti wa kisekta
pamoja na Tume ya Ushindani kama sehemu ya kufikia mkakati huu madhubuti ili
kushajiisha ushindani ndani ya nchi na uzingatiwaji wa misingi ya uendeshaji wa
uchumi wa soko.
Kukosekana kwa ushindani katika soko, huduma za ukuaji wa uchumi kwani
wawekezaji wengi hawatavutiwa kuwekeza kwenye masoko yasiyo na ushindani na
matokeo yake ni kulikosesha Taifa fursa za uwekezaji kunakosababisha
kukosekana kwa ajira na mapato kwa njia ya kodi mbalimbali.
Kwa upande mwingine, Kaulimbiu ya siku hii inasisitiza kuwa washindani
wanatakiwa kufanya shughuli zao BILA kula njama baina yao kwani kwa kufanya
hivyo husababisha bei ya bidhaa na huduma kuwa KUBWA pamoja na
kutengeneza UHABA wa bidhaa kwa mlaji jambo ambalo humuathiri mlaji. Jambo
hili husababisha washindani kushindwa kushindana katika masoko ya kikanda na
kimataifa jambo ambalo halileti tija katika uchumi wa nchi.
5

Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, FCC imepata mafanikio makubwa katika
utekelezaji wa Sheria ya Ushindani kama ilivyoelezwa na Mkurugenzi Mkuu wa
FCC.
Ili kuendeleza na kuboresha mafanikio hayo, Serikali imebaini kwamba kuna haja
na hoja za msingi za kuboresha nyenzo muhimu ya kufanikisha usimamizi wa
misingi ya ushindani katika soko na kumlinda mlaji vyema zaidi katika soko.
Nyenzo hiyo ni Sheria ya Ushindani Namba 8 ya mwaka 2003 ambayo kwa sasa
iko katika hatua za mwisho kufanyiwa marekebisho (amendment) ili kuipa nguvu
zaidi ya kushughulikia masuala ya ushindani na kumlinda mlaji.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, nimesikia changamoto mbalimbali za
kiushindani kutoka kwa wadau kama zilivyoelezewa na Mkurugenzi Mkuu. Sasa
naiagiza FCC kuhakikisha changamoto hizi zinatatuliwa kwa wakati ili kuleta ustawi
katika biashara zetu ikiwa ni pamoja na kusaidia ukuaji wa uchumi. Na hii ndio
sababu inayotufanya tuweke jitihada katika mabadiliko ya sheria ya Ushindani ili
kuhakikisha changamoto zote zinatatuliwa kwa wakati pasipo kukwamishwa na
mapungufu yaliyopo kwenye sheria ya sasa.
Ndugu washiriki na wageni waalikwa, nihitimishe hotuba yangu kwa kuwataka
wawakilishi wa wadau wafahamu na kuwafikishia ujumbe wenzao ambao
hawajapata fursa ya kuwa nasi pahala hapa kama ifuatavyo;
1. Madhumuni ya Serikali katika kusimamia uchumi wa soko si kukataza biashara
bali kutaka ifanyike kwa kuzingatia sheria na misingi ya ushindani.
2. Washindani wanatakiwa kushindana na si kula njama za kukwepa kushindana
sokoni, ili kutimiza malengo yaliyowekwa na sheria ikiwa ni pamoja na
kuhakikisha wananchi wanapata huduma zenye ubora, wanapata huduma katika
bei nzuri na wanakuwa na wigo mpana wa kuchagua bidhaa na huduma. Haya
yote yatawezekana iwapo tu tutafanya biashara zetu kwa kuzingatia misingi ya
ushindani. Washindani watumie fursa iliyopo kutatua migogoro inayohusu
ushindani baina yao kwa kutumia vyombo husika ambavyo vimewekwa kisheria
kama Tume ya Ushindani (FCC).
6

3. Tume ya Ushindani pamoja na vyombo vingine vinavyosimamia masuala ya
biashara, vitekeleze majukumu yao kwa kuongeza zaidi utoaji wa elimu kwa
wafanyabiashara na kuwaelekeza zaidi kuhusu yawapasayo kutenda ili kuepuka
uvunjwaji wa sheria. Aidha, niwashukuru na kuwapongeza sana wanahabari kwa
kujumuika nasi katika shughuli hii, hakika mnafanya kazi muhimu sana katika
kuuhabarisha Umma juu ya shughuli zinazofanywa na Serikali.
Baada ya kusema hayo, kwa heshima na taadhima, natamka kuwa
Maadhimisho ya Kitaifa ya Siku ya Ushindani Duniani yenye Kaulimbiu “Cartel
and their harmful effect on consumers” yaani “Njama baina ya washindani na
madhara yake kwa walaji na watumiaji” yamehitimishwa rasmi leo tarehe 5
Disemba, 2023.
MUNGU AWABARIKI, ASANTENI KWA KUNISIKILIZA.
Mhe. Dkt. Ashatu K. Kijaji (MB)
WAZIRI WA VIWANDA NA BIASHARA
Dar es Salaam, Desemba 5, 2023
Speech by Hon. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (MP), Minister for Industry and Trade,
during the World Competition Day Summit held at Serengeti Conference Hall,
Competition House, Dar es Salaam on December 5, 2023.
Chairman of the Fair Competition Commission (FCC), Dr. Aggrey Mlimuka,
Members of the Commission (FCC),
Director-General of the FCC, Mr. William Erio,
Director-General of the Tanzania Bureau of Standards, Dr. Athuman Y.
Ngenya,
CEO of the Tanzania Investment Centre, Mr. Gilead J. Teri,
CEO of the Business Registration and Licensing Agency (BRELA), Mr.
Godfrey Nyaisa,
Representatives of the East African Community Competition Authority,
Representatives of Trade Marks East Africa (TMEA),
CEO of the Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority,
7

CEO of the Small Industries Development Organization (SIDO),
CEO of the Weights and Measures Agency (WMA),
CEO of the National Development Corporation (NDC),
CEO of the Tanzania Investment Centre (TIC),
Management and Staff of the Fair Competition Commission,
Representatives from Ministries, Departments, and Government Institutions,
Representatives of small-scale miners from the Lake Zone,
Representatives of seed producers and distributors from the Northern Zone,
Representatives of grape and sunflower oil processors from the Central
Zone,
Representatives of industries and traders from the Southern Highlands Zone,
Representatives of cashew farmers from the Eastern Zone,
Distinguished guests,
Members of the press,
Ladies and Gentlemen,
I have the honour to express my gratitude to the Almighty God, full of mercy and
grace, for granting us good health and enabling us to come together to participate
in this important event commemorating the World Competition Day summit, held
nationally here in Dar es Salaam.
Secondly, I would like to thank the FCC for inviting me to these celebrations. I
commend them for the excellent organization and coordination of this World
Competition Day event. Well done!
Furthermore, I want to sincerely thank all stakeholders and invitees for responding
to the call to attend this crucial culmination of the World Competition Day
celebrations for the year 2023. Despite your other commitments, we appreciate
your presence.
Dear participants and invited guests, we all know that the purpose of any
business is to make and maximize profit. In pursuing this goal, various methods are
employed by businesses, including legitimate methods that promote innovation and
competition, as well as illegitimate methods that violate existing laws, rules, and
regulations. This is a significant challenge that negatively impacts business and the
economy as a whole.
In response to this challenge, the United Nations, through Decision No. 34/447 of
December 19, 1979, adopted the Multilaterally Agreed Equitable Principles and
Rules for the Control of Restrictive Business Practices during its meeting from April
8 to 22, 1980. Since then, these principles have been instrumental in the creation of
competition laws worldwide under the coordination of the United Nations
Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).
8

This laid the foundation for the establishment of World Competition Day
celebrations to commemorate the efforts to control practices that undermine
competition in global trade, held annually on December 5.
Dear participants and invited guests, practices that undermine competition, the
foundation of global competition law, can be categorized into the following groups:
1. Anti-Competitive Agreements: These include
a. Competitors meeting and fixing prices for goods and services;
b. Competitors agreeing on the quantity of goods produced (output restriction);
c. Competitors refusing to usher products to the market (collective boycott);
d. Competitors agreeing on how to bid when tenders are announced (bid rigging).
2. Abuse/misuse of market power by companies with significant market dominance.
3. Mergers of companies aimed at strengthening market dominance and affecting
competition and consumers in the market.
Dear participants and invited guests, each year during these celebrations, there
is a guiding theme. The theme for 2023 is "Prioritizing Socially Sensitive Sectors,"
which in Tanzania has been interpreted as "Cartels and their harmful effects on
consumers." This theme is timely as the world continues to grapple with the effects
of two major disasters, COVID-19 and the war in Ukraine and Russia, resulting in
rising prices of goods and services. This situation urges businesses to seek ways to
increase profits through various means, including cartels. This could have negative
effects on the nation's economy and hinder the efforts of the sixth-phase
government in achieving sustainable development for its citizens. I take this
opportunity, as the government, to urge businesses to avoid cartels, and the FCC,
as the regulatory authority, to closely monitor market conditions.
Dear participants and invited guests, I have been informed that as part of these
celebrations, the FCC conducted seminars for various stakeholders in the regions it
oversees, including:
(i) Small-scale miners in the Lake Zone;
(ii) Seed producers and distributors from the Northern Zone, Arusha;
(iii) Grape and sunflower oil processors from the FCC headquarters in Dodoma;
(iv) Industries and traders from the Southern Highlands Zone, Mbeya;
(iv) Cashew farmers from the Eastern Zone – Mtwara.
I have also been informed that representatives from each mentioned
region are present here, utilizing this opportunity to learn and witness
firsthand the challenges they face in their areas and how the FCC
addresses them according to existing laws and competition principles.
9

Dear participants and invited guests, competition law plays a crucial role in
building the economy. Conducting our businesses following the principles of
competition will bring the following benefits:
(i) Increased efficiency in the production and distribution of goods and services;
(ii) Promotion of innovation;
(iii) Improved use of resources by focusing on efficiency.
These benefits will enable us to compete in regional and international markets,
especially considering that Tanzania is already part of the African Continental Free
Trade Area (AfCFTA). Therefore, without following these principles, Tanzania may
become a market for products from other countries.
Dear participants and invited guests, I believe you have heard the insightful
details outlined by the Director-General of the FCC regarding the core
responsibilities carried out by the FCC in controlling and overseeing Tanzania's
mainland market to ensure that participants, especially competing businesses and
companies, adhere to competition principles and consumer rights.
The Director-General emphasized that engaging in cartel activities is not only
against competition law but also has significant negative effects on consumers.
Such practices make our companies uncompetitive regionally and internationally,
as they lack innovation and efficiency in production. As the government and the
leading ministry overseeing business in the country, we do not want to see
businesses engaging in price-fixing or controlling the quantity of goods released to
the market because it is against competition law, and when detected, legal action
will be taken.
Dear participants and invited guests, through the implementation of the Vision
2025 Development Plan, Tanzania has already set the direction to build a robust
and internationally competitive economy, aiming to achieve a better quality of life
for all. In line with these aspirations, the government established sectoral regulatory
bodies, including the Fair Competition Commission, as part of a comprehensive
strategy to promote competition within the country and adhere to the principles of a
market economy.
The absence of competition in the market hinders economic growth, as many
investors are not attracted to invest in non-competitive markets. This leads to
missed investment opportunities, resulting in a lack of employment opportunities
and revenue through various taxes.
On the other hand, the theme of this day emphasizes that competitors should
conduct their business without conspiring against each other. Engaging in such
conspiracies leads to higher prices of goods and services and creates a shortage of
products for consumers, adversely affecting them. This situation prevents
10

competitors from competing regionally and internationally, which is not beneficial to
the country's economy.
Dear participants and invited guests, the FCC has achieved significant success
in implementing the Competition Act, as outlined by the Director-General of the
FCC.
To continue and enhance these achievements, the government has identified the
need and valid reasons to improve the essential tools for implementing competition
principles in the market and better-protecting consumers. This tool is the
Competition Act No. 8 of 2003, which is currently in the final stages of being
amended to give it more power to address competition issues and protect
consumers.
Dear participants and invited guests, I have heard various competition-related
challenges from stakeholders, as explained by the Director-General. I now instruct
the FCC to ensure that these challenges are addressed promptly to promote
prosperity in our businesses and contribute to economic growth. This is why we are
investing efforts in amending the Competition Act to ensure that all challenges are
resolved without being hindered by the shortcomings in the current law.
Dear participants and invited guests, I conclude my speech by urging
representatives of stakeholders to understand and convey the message to their
colleagues who did not have the opportunity to be with us today:
1. The government's purpose in managing the market economy is not to prohibit
business but to ensure that it operates in accordance with the law and competition
principles.
2. Competitors should compete and not conspire to avoid competition in the market,
to achieve the goals set by the law, including ensuring that citizens receive quality
services at fair prices and have a wide range of choices. All this is possible if we
conduct our business according to competition principles. Competitors should use
the available opportunities to resolve disputes related to competition using the
appropriate legal channels, such as the Fair Competition Commission (FCC).
3. The Fair Competition Commission, along with other bodies overseeing business
issues, should fulfill their responsibilities by increasing education for businesses
and directing them more on what they should do to avoid legal violations. Hence, I
would like to express my gratitude and congratulations to the media for joining us in
this event; you are doing essential work in informing the public about the activities
carried out by the government.
After saying that, with respect and humility, I declare that the National Celebrations
of World Competition Day with the theme "Cartels and their harmful effects on
consumers" have officially winded up today, December 5, 2023.
11

MAY GOD BLESS YOU, THANK YOU FOR LISTENING.
Hon. Dr. Ashatu K. Kijaji (MP)
MINISTER OF INDUSTRY AND TRADE
Dar es Salaam, December 5, 2023

Secondly, I would like to thank the FCC for inviting me to these celebrations. I
commend them for the excellent organization and coordination of this World
Competition Day event. Well done!
Furthermore, I want to sincerely thank all stakeholders and invitees for responding

Dear participants and invited guests, we all know that the purpose of any
business is to make and maximize profit. In pursuing this goal, various methods are
employed by businesses, including legitimate methods that promote innovation and
competition, as well as illegitimate methods that violate existing laws, rules, and
regulations. This is a significant challenge that negatively impacts business and the
economy as a whole.
In response to this challenge, the United Nations, through Decision No. 34/447 of
December 19, 1979, adopted the Multilaterally Agreed Equitable Principles and
Rules for the Control of Restrictive Business Practices during its meeting from April
8 to 22, 1980. Since then, these principles have been instrumental in the creation of
competition laws worldwide under the coordination of the United Nations
Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).
8This laid the foundation for the establishment of World Competition Day
celebrations to commemorate the efforts to control practices that undermine
competition in global trade, held annually on December 5.
Dear participants and invited guests, practices that undermine competition, the
foundation of global competition law, can be categorized into the following groups:
1. Anti-Competitive Agreements: These include
a. Competitors meeting and fixing prices for goods and services;
b. Competitors agreeing on the quantity of goods produced (output restriction);
c. Competitors refusing to usher products to the market (collective boycott);
d. Competitors agreeing on how to bid when tenders are announced (bid rigging).
2. Abuse/misuse of market power by companies with significant market dominance.
3. Mergers of companies aimed at strengthening market dominance and affecting
competition and consumers in the market.
Dear participants and invited guests, each year during these celebrations, there
is a guiding theme. The theme for 2023 is "Prioritizing Socially Sensitive Sectors,"
which in Tanzania has been interpreted as "Cartels and their harmful effects on
consumers." This theme is timely as the world continues to grapple with the effects
of two major disasters, COVID-19 and the war in Ukraine and Russia, resulting in
rising prices of goods and services. This situation urges businesses to seek ways to
increase profits through various means, including cartels. This could have negative
effects on the nation's economy and hinder the efforts of the sixth-phase
government in achieving sustainable development for its citizens. I take this
opportunity, as the government, to urge businesses to avoid cartels, and the FCC,
as the regulatory authority, to closely monitor market conditions.
Dear participants and invited guests, I have been informed that as part of these
celebrations, the FCC conducted seminars for various stakeholders in the regions it
oversees, including:
(i) Small-scale miners in the Lake Zone;
(ii) Seed producers and distributors from the Northern Zone, Arusha;
(iii) Grape and sunflower oil processors from the FCC headquarters in Dodoma;
(iv) Industries and traders from the Southern Highlands Zone, Mbeya;
(iv) Cashew farmers from the Eastern Zone – Mtwara.
I have also been informed that representatives from each mentioned
region are present here, utilizing this opportunity to learn and witness
firsthand the challenges they face in their areas and how the FCC
addresses them according to existing laws and competition principles.
9Dear participants and invited guests, competition law plays a crucial role in
building the economy. Conducting our businesses following the principles of
competition will bring the following benefits:
(i) Increased efficiency in the production and distribution of goods and services;
(ii) Promotion of innovation;
(iii) Improved use of resources by focusing on efficiency.
These benefits will enable us to compete in regional and international markets,
especially considering that Tanzania is already part of the African Continental Free
Trade Area (AfCFTA). Therefore, without following these principles, Tanzania may
become a market for products from other countries.
Dear participants and invited guests, I believe you have heard the insightful
details outlined by the Director-General of the FCC regarding the core
responsibilities carried out by the FCC in controlling and overseeing Tanzania's
mainland market to ensure that participants, especially competing businesses and
companies, adhere to competition principles and consumer rights.
The Director-General emphasized that engaging in cartel activities is not only
against competition law but also has significant negative effects on consumers.
Such practices make our companies uncompetitive regionally and internationally,
as they lack innovation and efficiency in production. As the government and the
leading ministry overseeing business in the country, we do not want to see
businesses engaging in price-fixing or controlling the quantity of goods released to
the market because it is against competition law, and when detected, legal action
will be taken.
Dear participants and invited guests, through the implementation of the Vision
2025 Development Plan, Tanzania has already set the direction to build a robust
and internationally competitive economy, aiming to achieve a better quality of life
for all. In line with these aspirations, the government established sectoral regulatory
bodies, including the Fair Competition Commission, as part of a comprehensive
strategy to promote competition within the country and adhere to the principles of a
market economy.
The absence of competition in the market hinders economic growth, as many
investors are not attracted to invest in non-competitive markets. This leads to
missed investment opportunities, resulting in a lack of employment opportunities
and revenue through various taxes.
On the other hand, the theme of this day emphasizes that competitors should
conduct their business without conspiring against each other. Engaging in such
conspiracies leads to higher prices of goods and services and creates a shortage of
products for consumers, adversely affecting them. This situation prevents
10competitors from competing regionally and internationally, which is not beneficial to
the country's economy.
Dear participants and invited guests, the FCC has achieved significant success
in implementing the Competition Act, as outlined by the Director-General of the
FCC.
To continue and enhance these achievements, the government has identified the
need and valid reasons to improve the essential tools for implementing competition
principles in the market and better-protecting consumers. This tool is the
Competition Act No. 8 of 2003, which is currently in the final stages of being
amended to give it more power to address competition issues and protect
consumers.
Dear participants and invited guests, I have heard various competition-related
challenges from stakeholders, as explained by the Director-General. I now instruct
the FCC to ensure that these challenges are addressed promptly to promote
prosperity in our businesses and contribute to economic growth. This is why we are
investing efforts in amending the Competition Act to ensure that all challenges are
resolved without being hindered by the shortcomings in the current law.
Dear participants and invited guests, I conclude my speech by urging
representatives of stakeholders to understand and convey the message to their
colleagues who did not have the opportunity to be with us today:
1. The government's purpose in managing the market economy is not to prohibit
business but to ensure that it operates in accordance with the law and competition
principles.
2. Competitors should compete and not conspire to avoid competition in the market,
to achieve the goals set by the law, including ensuring that citizens receive quality
services at fair prices and have a wide range of choices. All this is possible if we
conduct our business according to competition principles. Competitors should use
the available opportunities to resolve disputes related to competition using the
appropriate legal channels, such as the Fair Competition Commission (FCC).
3. The Fair Competition Commission, along with other bodies overseeing business
issues, should fulfill their responsibilities by increasing education for businesses
and directing them more on what they should do to avoid legal violations. Hence, I
would like to express my gratitude and congratulations to the media for joining us in
this event; you are doing essential work in informing the public about the activities
carried out by the government.
After saying that, with respect and humility, I declare that the National Celebrations
of World Competition Day with the theme "Cartels and their harmful effects on
consumers" have officially winded up today, December 5, 2023.
